Mina — thanks for the packet. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Default timeout: our gateway currently uses 30s upstream timeouts. We can increase for testing but want to avoid breaking other services. Is 60s just for initial testing?
2) Retries: how do you recommend we handle streaming responses? We have some user flows that require partial streams and can’t easily deduplicate.
3) Procurement: looping our procurement lead here — procurement@saturnpay.com — to review the MAP.

If you can advise on streaming + timeout recommendations, we’ll provision a staging load test for next week.

—Alex
CTO, SaturnPay

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex@saturnpay.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@saturnpay.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding pact: SDK bootstrapping, timeout/quotas & migration checklist

Alex — thanks, good questions. Short answers with recommended patterns:

- Timeout guidance: 60s is intentionally conservative for early validation because model cold-starts and long-context prompts can exceed 30s. For production, after you enable streaming and prefix/KV caching, target 20–30s for synchronous calls. If you use streaming, keep the request-level timeout higher (45–60s) but enforce an idle timeout (e.g., 10s of no-chunk activity) to close stalled streams.

- Streaming & retries: avoid automatic retries for streaming requests. Instead:
  - Use resume tokens where possible (we support chunked resumption for long jobs in the SDK).
  - For non-resumable streams, implement client-side checkpointing so you can re-request from the last known stable state rather than retrying the same stream.

- Idempotency: include an idempotency-key header for generate requests that can be retried safely (we echo it in our logs for dedup).

- Rate limits: during staging load tests, increment concurrency in steps: 5 -> 25 -> 100 RPS, monitor 429s and tail-latency. If you see consistent 429s at 25 RPS, request a quota bump in the MAP and we’ll prioritize capacity.

I’ll attach a short streaming checklist to the MAP and loop in our implementation engineer to propose exact cutover timings.

Mina

Vanessa Ortiz
